title: Evidence manifest, schema version 2
description: CLAUDECODEBRIEF §7.2, informed by classification spec §14 (evidence retention tiers) and §23 (format families). One file per issue, listing every source cited and what was fetched/attested for it. Attestation (hash, timestamp) is always attempted; preservation (an archive copy) is attempted but its failure never blocks the entry. v2 (classification spec v4.2 amendment B) adds entries[].content_check, a length-heuristic flag on newly-fetched captures that a shell page (consent screen, login wall, empty client-rendered page) returned HTTP 200 with too little normalized text to plausibly contain an article. It is not the assertion-text match the amendment actually specifies -- that needs a claim's text, which this schema has no field for -- so it catches the common failure mode without claiming to catch the rest.

schema_version.description: Stamped by capture_evidence.py for the whole file, as of whichever version of the script last wrote it. 1: written before the content_check field existed. 2: written by a version of the script that stamps content_check on every newly-fetched entry -- individual entries already captured under v1 are carried forward unchanged rather than retroactively checked, since nobody re-verified them.

capture_is_retrospective.description: true where fetched is today's date rather than the issue's original publication date. CLAUDECODEBRIEF §9.

content_type.description: null where the response carried no Content-Type header at all -- a legitimate absence, not an empty string.

note.description: Why a non-captured attempt failed: a timeout, an HTTP error, a rate limit. capture_evidence.py records this on every failed/blocked attempt.

content_check.description: Length-heuristic shell-capture flag, scripts/capture_evidence.py, classification spec §5A. Absent on entries captured before this field existed (schema v1); present on every newly-fetched entry going forward.

manifest_sha256.description: sha256 of this file's own entries array, computed over a canonical serialization, excluding this field itself. Printed in the issue footer as the snapshot-in-time attestation.

timestamp.description: RFC 3161 / OpenTimestamps anchor on manifest_sha256. Hook only for now, per CLAUDECODEBRIEF appendix; not populated in this pass.
